title: Chapter 3 Quiz: Handling Events & User Input
description: Test your knowledge of event binding, modifiers, keyboard events, forms, and best practices.

questions.question: What is the shorthand for `v-on:click`?
questions.explanation: `@click` is the shorthand for `v-on:click`.

questions.question: Inline event handlers (e.g., `@click="count++"`) are always the best choice.
questions.explanation: Inline handlers are fine for simple expressions, but complex logic should be placed in methods to keep templates clean.

questions.question: Which modifier would you use to stop event propagation?
questions.explanation: `.stop` calls `event.stopPropagation()`.

questions.question: To prevent a form from reloading the page on submit, you use the modifier __________.
questions.explanation: `.prevent` calls `event.preventDefault()`, which stops the browser's default form submission.

questions.question: You can chain multiple modifiers like `@click.stop.prevent`.
questions.explanation: Yes, modifiers can be chained in any order.

questions.question: Which key modifier would you use to react to the Enter key?
questions.explanation: `.enter` is the built‑in alias for the Enter key.

questions.question: What does the `.once` modifier do?
options: Prevents the event from firing more than once
Calls the handler only once, then removes it
questions.explanation: `.once` ensures the event handler is executed at most one time.

questions.question: The `.self` modifier triggers the handler only if the event target is the element itself.
questions.explanation: `.self` is useful for preventing events from bubbling up from children.

questions.question: To capture Ctrl+Enter, you would use `@keyup.ctrl.__________`.
questions.explanation: You chain modifiers: `@keyup.ctrl.enter`.

questions.question: Which event is triggered when a form is reset by a reset button?
questions.explanation: `@reset` is triggered when a form is reset.

questions.question: The `@input` event is fired on every keystroke, while `@change` fires when the element loses focus after a change.
questions.explanation: Correct. `@input` is immediate, `@change` is on blur.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to use methods for complex event handling?
options: Because inline handlers cannot access component data
To keep templates declarative and maintainable
Because inline handlers are not supported in Vue 3
questions.explanation: Moving logic to methods improves readability, testability, and maintainability.

questions.question: The modifier that indicates the handler will never call `preventDefault()` (useful for scroll performance) is __________.
questions.explanation: `.passive` improves scrolling performance by telling the browser that the handler won't call `preventDefault()`.

questions.question: You can use system modifiers like `.ctrl` with mouse events as well.
questions.explanation: Yes, e.g., `@click.ctrl` will trigger only when Ctrl is held during the click.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to bind to the `keydown` event?
questions.explanation: Both `@keydown` and `v-on:keydown` are valid.

questions.question: To make an event handler fire only when the event target is the element itself, use the __________ modifier.
questions.explanation: `.self` ensures the handler is only called if the event originated from that exact element, not from a child.

questions.question: Event modifiers can be used with any DOM event, not just clicks.
questions.explanation: Yes, modifiers work with any event (keyboard, mouse, form events, etc.).

questions.question: What does the `.capture` modifier do?
options: Captures the event before it reaches the target
questions.explanation: `.capture` adds the event listener in capture mode, meaning it fires during the capture phase before the target phase.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common technique to improve performance for rapidly firing events like `@input`?
questions.explanation: Both debouncing (delay execution) and throttling (limit rate) are used to optimize high‑frequency events.

questions.question: You can use `v-on` to listen to custom events emitted by child components.
questions.explanation: Yes, `v-on` works for both DOM events and custom component events (we'll cover that in components chapter).
